connector.title: MCP connection
connector.hint: External AI can read and analyze the open transcript and its original comparison on request. Before editing, it asks whether to save a new version or update the current editable version. It can also add AI annotations and highlights to the current version. Access is limited to the open transcript. No audio is sent; transcript text is sent to the selected AI service when requested.
connector.ready: Local connection ready. Finish adding and enabling Ripple in the selected AI application before using it.
connector.error: The connection isn’t ready. Check the selected AI application’s configuration, then try again.
connector.setup_saved: Configuration saved. You can enable the connection.
connector.setup_error: Configuration incomplete. Check the tunnel client, Tunnel ID, and Runtime API key.
connector.configured: Configuration saved. You can enable the connection.
connector.softwareHint: Choose the software whose setup you want to view. Configured connections work independently; switching this list does not disconnect them.
connector.claudeStep1: Click “Add to Claude” to open the extension installer.
connector.claudeStep2: Confirm the Ripple installation in Claude. You don’t need to edit the configuration manually.
connector.workbuddyStep1: Choose “Add to WorkBuddy”, then confirm the connection.
connector.workbuddyStep2: Ripple backs up your existing configuration before adding the connection. In WorkBuddy, open “Experts · Skills · Connectors → Connectors → Custom connectors”, find Ripple, and enable it. If Ripple doesn’t appear, restart WorkBuddy and check again.
connector.localStep3: Keep Ripple open and enable the MCP connection, then select Ripple in your AI conversation.
connector.added_claude: Claude’s extension installer is open. Confirm the Ripple installation, then use Ripple in a conversation.
connector.added_workbuddy: Connection configuration added to WorkBuddy. Open “Experts · Skills · Connectors → Connectors → Custom connectors”, find Ripple, and enable it. If Ripple doesn’t appear, restart WorkBuddy and check again. Once Ripple is enabled, you can ask for it directly in a conversation without selecting it from the “+” menu.
connector.added_chatgpt: ChatGPT’s plugins page is open. Follow step 4 to add and install the plugin, then use Ripple in a conversation.
connector.addError_workbuddy: Couldn’t add Ripple to WorkBuddy. Check that WorkBuddy’s configuration is valid and isn’t being edited, then try again. Don’t delete existing connections.
connector.addError_claude: Couldn’t open the installer. Make sure Claude Desktop is installed, then try again.
connector.addError_chatgpt: Couldn’t open the browser. Open https://chatgpt.com/plugins manually.
connector.tunnelCopied: Tunnel ID copied. Choose Tunnel as the connection method in ChatGPT, then paste the ID.
connector.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy the Tunnel ID. Copy it manually from the field above.
connector.workbuddyStep3: Keep Ripple open with the MCP connection enabled. After enabling Ripple in WorkBuddy, you can ask for it directly in a conversation without selecting it from the “+” menu.
connector.chatgptTransportPending: The ChatGPT tunnel is not ready. Check its connection settings below; other configured AI software can still connect.
connector.guidedTunnel: Create or select a tunnel in <setupLink>OpenAI tunnel settings</setupLink>, then paste its Tunnel ID here.
connector.guidedKey: Create a key with tunnel read and use permissions (Tunnels · Read / Use) on the <setupLink>OpenAI API keys page</setupLink>, then paste it here.
connector.guidedClient: Extract it, click “Choose tunnel client”, then select tunnel-client.
connector.guidedClientWindows: Extract it, click “Choose tunnel client”, then select tunnel-client.exe.
connector.guidedClientUnknown: Choose the full archive for your operating system and chip, extract it, then select the client.
connector.guidedChatGPT: In ChatGPT, choose “+ → Add custom MCP server”. Name it Ripple, choose Tunnel and the same tunnel, and set Authentication to No authentication. Review the risk notice, create the plugin, then install it.
connector.guidedPending: Save the configuration and enable MCP connection. Wait for the tunnel to be ready before continuing.
connector.keepSavedKey: Leave this field blank to keep the saved key.
connector.savePrerequisite: Complete the first three steps, then save
connector.device_unknown: Not identified yet; choose your operating system and chip
connector.release_missing: No full archive for this computer was found in the latest release. Check the official downloads page.
connector.release_failed: The latest release is unavailable. Check again or open the official downloads page.
connector.macAuthorizationTitle: Mac says the program cannot be verified?
connector.macAuthorization: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Allow Anyway (or Open Anyway). Confirm, then return to Ripple and reconnect.
connector.existingConnectionTitle: Already have Ripple, or is the name taken?
connector.existingConnection: After changing tunnels, add a new custom connection. If the name is taken, use “Ripple new connection”. Reconnecting the old plugin does not change its tunnel.
connector.openLinkError: Could not open the browser. Copy this address and open it manually: {{url}}
connector.aiSetupTitle: Want AI to help with setup?
connector.aiSetupHint: If your ChatGPT or Codex can operate this computer and browser, give it the request below. You still need to confirm sign-in and permissions.
connector.aiSetupPrompt:
Follow the official OpenAI guide to connect Ripple on this computer to ChatGPT: create or reuse a tunnel, download the full tunnel-client archive for this computer, prepare a connection key, save the configuration in Ripple, then add a custom MCP plugin using the same tunnel. Ask me when sign-in or confirmation is needed. Keep keys out of chat. Finish with a read-only tool call without modifying transcripts.
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels
